reviews.title: Firefox Very Very Lite
reviews.text:
Got this after the recent Firefox desktop update, Firefox for iPhone is very basic. If you’re expecting the same experience as the desktop version then don’t bother, no bookmark management. 

Firstly, there is no direct way to import bookmarks that are in another browser on your iPhone, no way to rename bookmark folders or move bookmarks to other folders.

It’s presumed you have a desktop device, where you export your bookmarks from Safari or DuckDuckGo browser running on your iPhone and airdrop or email the bookmarks to your desktop device running Firefox, import them into Firefox and then Sync the iPhone with your desktop. 

I run a different set of bookmarks on my laptop, compared with those on my iPhone. The lack of bookmark management and choice of which bookmarks are Synced makes Firefox for iPhone difficult to use.


 Sadly back to Safari and DuckDuckGo 
:-(

Look forward to an improved version…

reviews.title: Looks pretty but not fun to use
reviews.text: This is the 6th go with Firefox for iOS. All previous trials were fails,the app was too light weight. As I use Firefox as my default browser on my Mac, I really want iOS Firefox to work. It’s not great as it’s easy to see all the restrictions associated with using Apple's WebKit. However, it’s fast, hasn’t skipped a beat in 2 days of heavy usage on all sorts of sites but has some serious usage issues: 1), the UI is terrible, simple access to bookmarks is buried at least 4 taps down before you get to your folders. My fingers ache from managing tabs. 2), The shortcuts page can’t be configured unless an item you want appears on it and, then can’t be named or placed where you want it. Basically an unidentifiable mess of icons. 3), There’s no download manager. 4), There's no cookie manager. 5), The adblocking is primitive and compared to my Firefox (Mac), Safari (iOS) or iCab (iOS) installs blocks little to nothing. My disappointment is Mozilla knows how to do good browsers. This is a poor product that a high school programming class could have bettered in a couple of weeks. Another fail, but better than the last.

reviews.title: Broken on 4 GB iPhones
reviews.text:
I’ve been using Firefox on all my devices for years, and that’s the main reason I use it on my iPhone too. I’ve always loved it, and until recently I never had any major issues.

However, the last few updates have made Firefox almost unusable on iPhones with 4 GB of RAM or less, even though those devices are still officially supported and continue to receive iOS updates from Apple. It constantly hangs, freezes, and becomes unresponsive. I use the exact same Firefox account on an iPhone with 8 GB of RAM, and it runs perfectly there, so the issue seems to be specific to lower-memory devices. I don’t understand why, either—I haven’t noticed any major new features that would explain such a significant drop in performance.

It’s really disappointing because Firefox has been my browser of choice across all my devices. If this isn’t fixed, I’ll have to stop using Firefox altogether and move to something else. The seamless sync between devices is the reason I use it in the first place, so if it no longer works reliably on my iPhone, there’s no reason for me to stay.

reviews.title: regretting updating to latest version
reviews.text:
New update has left the browser incredibly laggy and unresponsive, forcing me to completely close out and restart frequently in order to continue use. Where opening a new tab and attempting to search something used to be relatively instant, it now takes multiple seconds and very often does not actually result in a search loading, just the browser freezing and forcing me to quit and restart. Likewise with the tab view; clicking into a different open tab either freezes for a short time or seizes up the app.

The meatball menu icon now opening into a separate popup is much more inconvenient for quick access to eg:, find on page and settings seem far less comprehensive than they used to (another recent review even has a response from the developer suggesting a setting that doesn't seem even exist to make changes to the address bar). 

Incredibly disappointing experience. I have been checking back frequently to see if a new bug fix update has been released but nothing yet. In the meantime I will be looking for an alternate browser app and hope these issues are eventually fixed.

reviews.title: A total faff and a disappointment.
reviews.text:
Pretty disappointed. Use Firefox as my default browser on my PC. Was remote today armed only with my iPhone and needed to access something from my history. Of course, installing Firefox is easy, logging into my profile less so. I vaguely recall the overboard paranoid levels of security for my profile when setting up the PC. What I hadn’t expected was Firefox expects you to either remember the “difficult password” you’re encouraged to use and store in your PC’s password manager “for convenience”. 

What I hadn’t anticipated was if I can’t remember a randomly generated 32 character password or ridiculously complex “key” Firefox urges you to print and keep safe (which you… AT HOME)… the app allows you to access your account (having provided not one but TWO SEPARATE verification codes one via an Authenticator app) it erases all of your history… which was the whole point of this exercise in the first place. 

What the hell do you think you’re protecting Mozilla???!

It’s a chuffin’ WEB BROWSER of a person needs their browser history to be THIS secure I would hazard you PROBABLY don’t NEED them as a customer  because you probably don’t want to be complicit in whatever they’re trying to hide. 

Get some perspective.

reviews.title: History doesn't clear, tabs can't autoclose, and fandom wikia is unsuable
reviews.text:
I regret using this browser for as long as I did after trying out other ones. Despite it probably being the fastest ios browser, it has several bugs and lacks features most other browsers have. Here are its dealbreakers for me:

History just doesn’t clear. Despite pressing the clear history button, it never works, and there’s no option to have it clear at certain intervals.

Tabs can’t auto-close at intervals either. This is something virtually every browser, both on mobile and desktop (include Firefox, which can close tabs whenever you close the browsers) have. Yet the ios version doesn’t have it. Because I’m not used to having to remember to manually close them, they build up and it just gets on my nerves.

Fandom wikia pages never fully load and are stuck in a perpetual reloading cycle. I know fandom is a terrible site filled with bloatware and ads, but unfortunately I have to consult it on some very large video games that simply don’t use any alternatives. But because wikia site elements just don’t load, or because they reload every few seconds forcing you back to the top of the page, browsing wikia on firefox ios is genuinely a living nightmare. I have not had this problem on any other ios browser so I don’t understand why firefox has issues with it.

I guess if you don't have problems with any of the above then this IS the best ios browser...
